title: Car Pooling
statement: The car drives east only, never turning back. Each trip [passengers, from, to] picks that many people up at from and sets them down at to. Return whether every trip can be served without ever exceeding the capacity.
constraints: passengers get off AT the drop point, so a trip ending at x frees seats for a trip starting at x
hints: Only the points where the load changes matter, and there are at most 1001 of them.
A difference array over the locations: add passengers at from, subtract at to. Then one running total across it gives the load everywhere.

The drop-off convention is the whole trap. Subtracting at to rather than at to+1 is what makes a trip ending at x free its seats for one starting at x - get that backwards and back-to-back trips fail incorrectly.

cases.name: one trip ends where the next begins
a single trip already exceeds capacity
